text:
Claude Giroux is 38, with 1,165 career points entering this season, and the argument about his Hall of Fame case has already started (Broad Street Buzz reported last week that one Hall of Famer thinks he belongs). What keeps the case interesting is that he's still good.

Ottawa gets 60% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, and his relative number is well above his teammates. He has 15 points in 27 games on under 17 minutes a night, scoring at 2.0 points per 60, right around league average for forwards. His six goals on 4.94 expected look honest.

The Senators have won seven of his last ten, and he had a goal and an assist in Friday's 6-2 win in Tampa. He also scored early against Philadelphia on November 19, the team he captained for years and played 1,000 games for. Evolving-Hockey had him 47th among 401 forwards last season at 2.1 wins above replacement, with his defensive impact in the 89th percentile. Watch the ice time: he dipped to 12.8 minutes in Florida, and at his age, how Travis Green manages his workload matters as much as the points.
